From the methodological point of view, it is important to underscore: the present monograph fixes the structure of the tokenomics as a fact of the digital artifact requiring description, but does not act as an investment recommendation or an economic analysis.

NFT-reputation

A further technical instrument realising the social architecture is the system of NFT-reputation. The belonging of a participant to one of the four classes (Architects, Builders, Residents, Collectors), like his or her specific merits in the development of the ecosystem, is fixed in the form of non-fungible digital tokens (NFTs). This fixation secures:

transparency — any participant may verify the status of an interlocutor without the mediation of an administrator;

portability — reputation is not bound to a concrete platform and may be presented within any compatible interface;

protection against inflation — each NFT is unique and may not be arbitrarily copied;

connection with behaviour — the growth of reputation is possible only through actual actions within the ecosystem, not through financial investment.

A detailed technical-economic description of DarAi and of the NFT-reputation system lies beyond the bounds of the present monograph and belongs to a separate publication devoted to the Web3 component of the ecosystem.

A part of the revenues from the monetisation of YupLand is directed back into the development of the ecosystem itself. This unspoken agreement between the Architects and the participants of the ecosystem reflects the principle of mutual exchange and secures the sustainable development of the project without the concentration of resources on a single side.

The contour of ethical artificial intelligence

Within the ecosystem there is developed a separate direction — ethical artificial intelligence upon the basis of the YupLabs community, understood by the authors of the project as a threefold concordance: the ethics of the creator, the ethics of the user, and the ethics of the AI-entity itself. This formula stands opposed to the reduction — widespread in international practice — of the ethics of AI to a set of technical limitations and rules of safety. Within the YupLand ecosystem, ethics is regarded as a cross-cutting quality manifesting itself at all levels — from the orientations of the designer to the modes of the user’s interaction with the system.

The development of ethical AI within YupLabs passes through several stages:

The philosophical club — the invitation to dialogue of scholarly luminaries, international opinion leaders of the field, and visionaries; the discussion of existing conceptual frameworks; the elaboration of new ones.

The basic prototype — the creation of agents on existing language models (DeepSeek, GigaChat, ChatGPT, and others) capable of interacting with the user in the logic of ethical communication.

The neural model — the elaboration of a proprietary language model on a Cyrillic-based core, laid down as the foundation for a subsequent full-fledged AI-contour of the ecosystem.

The full-fledged ethical AI — a system securing the transmission of the thought-image from the operator with a minimal prompt or without one, elaborated within the logic of the methodology of “the ethics of the user of AI.”

From the methodological point of view, the present monograph fixes the contour of ethical AI as one of the directions of the development of the ecosystem, requiring a separate philosophical-methodological and empirical description in the future.

8.5. Modes of Embodiment of the Typological Model within the Product Contours

The present section describes the key particularity of YupLand from the philosophical-methodological point of view: the modes by which the noumenal structure of the Dar model becomes an observable artifact within the digital environment.

Algorithmic embodiment

The first and basic mode of embodiment is the algorithmic computation of the archetype. The declared typological structure is embodied in a deterministic function mapping the user’s biographical parameters into the triadic code. This function is:

fixed (one and the same input always yields one and the same output);

verifiable (each step of the computation is reproducible);

observable (the user receives a visible result of the computation).

Algorithmic embodiment transforms the noumenal classification into an operational object accessible to empirical investigation.

Content embodiment

The second mode is the content filling-out of each archetype in the form of structured descriptions. Each description (see Chapters 5–7) rests upon a unified template of 9 sections, securing the comparability of the archetypes among themselves. The noumenal structure (the classification) thereby acquires a corpus of observable linguistic material that the user may read, discuss, contest.

Interactive embodiment

The third mode is the user’s interactive experience within the ecosystem. The archetype does not remain a text upon a page; the user receives the possibility to interact with his or her Dar through the application, through AI-messages, through gaming contours, through social interactions. The noumenal structure thereby engenders behavioural patterns that likewise become material for observation.

Social embodiment

The fourth mode is the social anchoring of the archetype within the community. Users of YupLand come to know their archetype, discuss it with others, identify their patterns of interaction as typologically coloured. The archetype becomes a language of self-description — the means through which a participant of the community articulates his or her particularity.

Economic embodiment

The fifth mode is the economic operationalisation through the internal currency DarAi and the mechanics of giving. The user’s activity within the ecosystem is converted into observable economic flows that may be analysed as a quantitative indicator of engagement.

Each of the five modes produces its own class of phenomena — that which, in the categories of Chapter 2, was termed the “phenomenological level” in relation to the noumenal structure of the model.

8.6. YupLand as an Object of Scholarly Observation

The architecture described and the modes of embodiment render YupLand a unique object of empirical investigation. In distinction from typological classifications existing only as theoretical constructs or as a corpus of scholarly publications, YupLand contains a complete observational infrastructure:

a fixed algorithm of computation (the researcher has access to the deterministic procedure of assigning the user to an archetype);

a structured corpus of descriptions (the researcher may analyse the content of the archetypes as linguistic material);

behavioural data of users (with their consent and in anonymised form);

social dynamics (in the form of discussions, the exchange of experience, reflection);

economic indicators (in the form of flows of activity).

This transforms YupLand into a natural research platform — not only a product environment but a site upon which a scholarly programme for the study of the phenomena of digital typological identity may unfold.

The ethical frameworks of investigation

The use of YupLand as a research platform requires the strict observance of ethical principles:

the informed consent of users to participation in the research;

the separation of the research contour (the platform nauka-yupdar.vercel.app) from the product contour (the YupDar application), in order to prevent the conflation of motivations;

the anonymisation of data prior to scholarly processing;

the possibility of withdrawal from the research at any stage without consequences for the use of the ecosystem;

the transparency of aims and methods — the publication of the research design and the resulting findings in open access.

A detailed description of the research procedure is presented in Chapter 9.

Limitations of the approach

The consideration of YupLand as an object of scholarly observation is bound up with a number of limitations requiring discussion:

Selection bias — users of YupLand self-select on the basis of interest in the Dar system, which limits the generalisability of the findings.

The effect of the measurement artifact — the very participation in the ecosystem forms within the user expectations that influence his or her reactions.

The double role of the author. S. N. Nesterova is at once the author of the system and the developer of the application; however, the researcher in the proper sense is A. V. Makaeva, which excludes the developer’s influence upon the process and the result, and in large measure neutralises the “double role of the author.”

Technological dependencies — the functioning of the platform depends upon external providers (hosting, AI models, the messenger), and this affects the reproducibility of results over time.

These limitations are discussed at length in Chapter 10 as the methodological frame of the present work.

8.7. The Evolutionary Stages of the Ecosystem’s Development

For the completeness of the picture, we present the conception, agreed by the authors of the project, of the evolutionary stages of the development of the YupLand ecosystem. This is not a plan in the strict sense, but a reconstruction of the path already passed and of the projected directions, presented in a form convenient for scholarly description.

2024–2025

The development of the community; the transition to blockchain; the synergy of blockchain technologies and collective consciousness through the practices of the Dar system; the creation of products of the ecosystem and of game design; the launch of a platform for cooperation with business and science.

2. Development

2025–2026

The introduction of the referral system into all products; the introduction of a grants system for research teams; the development of the incubation hub; the creation of the archive of the “living data” of the community; the first MVP of ethical AI.

3. Scaling

2027–2028

Partnership with scholarly institutions in the fields of neuro-technologies and the ethics of AI; the formation of stable sub-ecosystems; the launch of a franchise of ecosystem solutions for external markets; the listing of DarAi upon major exchanges.

4. Autonomy

2029 and beyond

The ecosystem as a reference for projects in the logic of ethical technologies; full self-sufficiency; the establishment of DarAi as a standard for inter-project settlements; the launch of a long-term fund for the support of ethical AI initiatives.

From the methodological point of view, it is important to underscore that the present monograph does not assess the attainability of the declared project aims and does not act as an investment or marketing document. The stages are presented here as the historical and project context within which the phenomena of the embodiment of the Dar model — described in the principal part of the chapter — unfold.

In the present chapter, the YupLand digital ecosystem has been considered as an artifact of the embodiment of the noumenal structure of the Dar model. Described are: the history and ideology of the project; the cultural code and the figure of Yupik as the digital double; the social architecture (Architects / Builders / Residents / Collectors), the technological foundation, and the companion products of the ecosystem; the YupDar application as the point of entry into the system; the organisational-economic foundation in the form of the Principle of Dar-Giving, the cryptocurrency DarAi, the NFT-reputation system, and the contour of ethical artificial intelligence; the five modes of embodiment of the typological model within the product contours — algorithmic, content, interactive, social, economic; the methodological consequences of the consideration of YupLand as an object of scholarly observation; and the evolutionary stages of the ecosystem’s development from the preparatory phase of 2020–2023 to the projected autonomy. It has been shown that the YupLand ecosystem contains a complete research infrastructure permitting the transition from the theoretical description of the typological model to the empirical study of its phenomena.

chapters.title: Chapter 9. An Empirical Study of the Phenomenon of User Self-Recognition in a Personal Archetype
chapters.html:
The empirical part of the present monograph is devoted to the investigation of a single, but methodologically central, phenomenon of the embodiment of the Dar model within the digital environment: the phenomenon of user self-recognition in the personal archetype. By self-recognition here is understood the psychological act in the course of which the user, having become acquainted with the description of the archetype computed for him or her, recognises within it essential features of his or her own experience.

This phenomenon is chosen as the object of investigation for definite reasons: it manifests itself directly within the digital environment and may therefore be captured by standard survey methods; it possesses a rich tradition of methodological discussion — in the first instance in connection with the Barnum–Forer effect — which permits the embedding of the present work within a wide scholarly context; its measurement furnishes a minimally sufficient empirical basis for the evaluation of one of the key claims of the model: that an archetype is not a universal description applicable to anyone, but an individually differentiated pattern.

Within the present chapter are successively presented: the formulation of the research questions and hypotheses; the design of the investigation; the description of the sample and the recruitment procedure; the instrumentation and the protocol of data collection; the methodological controls; the plan of data analysis; the ethical foundations of the work; and the current status of the investigation and the preliminary results of the pilot phase.

9.1. Research Questions and Hypotheses

RQ1. Do users distinguish the description of their own archetype from the descriptions of other archetypes of the Dar system at a level above chance?

This question is key to the assessment of the empirical consistency of the model’s claim concerning the individual differentiation of archetypes. If the answer is positive, the claim receives initial empirical confirmation. If the answer is negative, this serves as a signal for the revision of the model, or for the differentiation of its noumenal claim from its phenomenological observability.

Auxiliary research questions

RQ2. What factors (the user’s biographical parameters, the particularities of the archetype itself, the context of acquaintance with the system) influence the intensity of self-recognition?

RQ3. What are the qualitative particularities of the phenomenon of self-recognition? Which concrete elements of the archetype’s description are recognised by users as “their own,” and which as “foreign” or neutral?

RQ4. Are the observed patterns reproduced upon a repeat survey after a definite temporal interval (test-retest reliability)?

The principal hypothesis

H1 (principal). The proportion of users recognising the description of their own archetype as “substantively fitting” (on the operationalised scale, see § 9.4) is statistically significantly greater than the proportion of users recognising as “substantively fitting” the description of a randomly assigned foreign archetype.

The null hypothesis H0: the indicated proportions are not statistically distinct (the proportion of self-recognition in the own archetype equals the proportion of self-recognition in the random foreign archetype).

Auxiliary hypotheses

H2. There exists a positive relation between the intensity of the user’s prior acquaintance with the Dar system and the intensity of self-recognition (a necessary control for the interpretation of results in the categories of user expectations).

H3. The structure of the archetype (basic, integral, special 9-9-9) influences the intensity of self-recognition: integral archetypes and the 9-9-9 archetype may exhibit a different pattern of responses by virtue of their specificity (see Chapters 6–7).

9.2. The Design of the Investigation

The investigation is constructed according to a mixed-methods design, including:

a quantitative component — a standardised questionnaire with closed scales for the verification of the principal and auxiliary hypotheses;

a qualitative component — open-ended questions permitting the fixation of the substantive content of the phenomenon of self-recognition.

Methodologically, we work within the recognition paradigm (the paradigm of differentiating recognition) rather than the classical self-assessment of correspondence. This paradigm presupposes that each participant:

becomes acquainted with the description of his or her own archetype;

becomes acquainted also with the description of a randomly selected foreign archetype (the control description);

evaluates both descriptions on an identical scale;

does not know which description pertains to him or her personally and which does not (a double-blind presentation).

The comparison of the evaluations of the own and the control descriptions permits the neutralisation of the Barnum–Forer effect (the classical effect of accepting any commonly intelligible typological description as “one’s own”). Were the Barnum effect the principal factor, the evaluations of the own and the control descriptions would not differ. A difference of evaluations indicates a specific recognisability of one’s own archetype.

The structure of the procedure

The procedure of the investigation contains the following stages:

The stage of entry. The user registers on the research platform nauka-yupdar.vercel.app, receives detailed information about the aims and methods of the investigation, gives informed consent.

The stage of collection of biographical parameters. The user enters the date, time, and place of birth, and the full name, for the computation of the individual archetype.

The stage of computation. The algorithm generates the individual profile (the triadic code).

The stage of blind presentation. The platform presents two descriptions: the user’s own archetype and a randomly assigned foreign archetype. The descriptions are presented in randomised order, without indication of which is “one’s own.”

The stage of evaluation. The user evaluates each description on an identical scale of self-recognition (see § 9.4).

The stage of qualitative unfolding. The user answers a series of open-ended questions concerning which elements of the descriptions appeared close, foreign, or neutral.

The stage of disclosure. The platform discloses which of the descriptions was the user’s own archetype, and proposes a final reflection.

The stage of repeat survey (after 4–6 weeks). A portion of the participants is invited a second time for the verification of test-retest reliability.

In order to exclude the order effect (the first description is evaluated differently from the second), the order of presentation of the own and the control descriptions is randomised at the individual level.

9.3. Sample and Recruitment Procedure

The target population of the investigation is adult users (18+ years) of the Russian-speaking internet who have voluntarily acquainted themselves with the invitation to participate in the research. This is a self-selected (convenience) sample, which constitutes a substantial methodological limitation (see § 9.5).

On the basis of a preliminary power calculation (with an anticipated medium effect size d ≈ 0.3, level of significance α = 0.05, and power 1 − β = 0.80), the minimum sample volume is estimated at 300 participants for the verification of the principal hypothesis. For the qualitative component, the minimally sufficient sample comprises 30–50 substantively unfolded answers to the open-ended questions.

The desired final sample volume is 500–800 participants, which secures the possibility of conducting comparative analyses by subgroups (auxiliary hypotheses H2, H3).

The recruitment of participants proceeds through:

the existing community of users of the YupLand ecosystem (with separation of the research and product contours);

specialised thematic communities on social networks (psychological, philosophical, typological);

academic channels (invitations through colleagues and partner organisations);

open invitations through the project’s presentation site.

Inclusion criteria: age 18+, command of the Russian language at the level of fluent reading and written response, voluntary consent.

Exclusion criteria: the presence of evident contradictions in the survey data; non-completion of the principal part of the survey; signs of automated responses (identified by standard procedures of data quality control).

9.4. Instrumentation and the Protocol of Data Collection

The principal instrument of the investigation is the scale of self-recognition, elaborated for the present study with consideration of existing recommendations on the measurement of typological recognition. The scale consists of 8 items, each evaluated on a 7-point Likert scale (from 1 — “completely does not fit” — to 7 — “completely fits”):

The description corresponds to my understanding of my own personality.

I recognise within the description concrete episodes of my life.

The weaknesses enumerated in the description are familiar to me.

The strengths enumerated in the description are familiar to me.

The motto of the archetype resonates with my inner experience.

The description discloses something about myself that I had not formulated before.

I would recommend this description to one who wishes to understand me.

On the whole, I recognise myself in the description.

The sum of the scores yields an integral indicator of self-recognition (range 8–56). For each participant, two such indicators are recorded: for the own archetype and for the control.

For the control of the Barnum–Forer effect, a separate scale is used, evaluating the extent to which the description is perceived as “universal, fitting to the majority of people” (4 items, 7-point Likert scale). High scores on this scale indicate that the participant is inclined to accept the description as universally applicable; the difference of evaluations between the own and the control descriptions remains, nevertheless, a significant indicator of specific recognisability.

The biographical and contextual block

The following are additionally collected:

biographical parameters (age, gender, education, professional sphere);

the duration and intensity of prior acquaintance with the Dar system (from “first acquaintance” to “many years of practice”);

a general disposition to reflection (a short questionnaire of 5 items);

current psychological condition (1 self-assessment item).

Within the protocol there is also a series of open-ended questions revealing the qualitative particularities of self-recognition:

Which concrete formulations within the description seemed to you most accurate with respect to yourself personally?

What within the description seemed to you altogether not yours?

What emotions did you experience while reading the description of your own archetype?

Did your relation to anything in your own life change after the reading of the description?

The open-ended answers are analysed by the method of thematic coding.

The digital platform

Data collection is conducted through a specialised digital platform, nauka-yupdar.vercel.app, elaborated within the framework of the present investigation. The platform secures:

the automatic computation of the individual archetype;

the automatic random selection of the control archetype;

the randomisation of the order of presentation;

the standardised collection of quantitative and qualitative data;

the export of an anonymised dataset for further processing.

The technological foundation of the platform corresponds to the general architecture of the YupLand ecosystem (see Chapter 8), but the research contour is formally separated from the product contour: participation in the investigation brings the user no intra-product advantages, and the data are not used for commercial purposes.

9.5. Methodological Controls

Control of the Barnum–Forer effect

This is realised through the double-blind presentation of the own and the control descriptions, and through a separate scale of the Barnum effect.

Control of user expectations

This is realised through the collection of data on prior acquaintance with the Dar system and the analysis of this variable as a possible moderator in the verification of the hypotheses.

Control of selection bias

The self-selection of users limits the generalisability of the findings. In order partially to compensate for this limitation, the analysis incorporates the following:

the description of the sample is presented in detail, so that the reader may assess the degree of its representativeness;

the verification of the principal hypothesis is supplemented by an analysis by subgroups (for example, among users encountering the Dar system for the first time vs. experienced practitioners);

the discussion of the limitations of the sample is presented in the results section.

Control of the role of the author

The double role of S. N. Nesterova (author of the system — developer of the platform) is neutralised through the implementation of preemptive measures:

the direct researcher is the co-author A. V. Makaeva; the processing of data is conducted with the participation of the co-author and of independent reviewers;

the research platform is separated from the product platform;

the anonymised dataset and the code of analysis are published in open access upon the completion of the investigation;

independent researchers are invited to reproduce the analysis.

Control of data quality

This is realised through standard procedures:

verification for duplicate records;

analysis of response time (exclusion of cases of evidently non-reading answers);

attention-check items (item-attention checks);

comparison of responses to reverse-coded item pairs.

9.6. The Plan of Data Analysis

The distributions of all key variables are described by standard indices: mean, median, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis. Categorical variables are presented in the form of frequency tables.

The principal hypothesis is verified through a paired comparative test of the self-recognition evaluations for the own vs. control descriptions. A paired-samples t-test (under the condition of normality of distribution) or its non-parametric equivalent (the Wilcoxon test) is used in the case of substantial deviations. Additionally, the effect size (Cohen’s d) is computed for the assessment of the practical significance of the result.

For hypothesis H2 (the relation of the intensity of self-recognition to prior acquaintance) — correlational and regression analysis.

For hypothesis H3 (differences across the classes of archetypes) — one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with post-hoc tests.

For the subsample of participants who completed the repeat survey, the coefficient of test-retest correlation is computed for the integral indicator of self-recognition. The desired threshold is r ≥ 0.70.

The open-ended answers are analysed by the method of thematic analysis with the participation of two independent coders. The consistency of coding is assessed by Cohen’s kappa coefficient. The themes revealed in the analysis are presented in the form of illustrated brief descriptions with direct citations from the anonymised answers.

9.7. The Ethical Foundations of the Investigation

Each participant, prior to the beginning of the investigation, receives unfolded information about:

the aims and objectives of the investigation;

the order of conduct of the procedure;

the character of the data collected;

the means of storage and use of the data;

the possibility of withdrawal from participation at any stage without consequences;

the contacts of the research group for questions and feedback.

Consent is recorded electronically prior to the beginning of the survey.

All data are stored in anonymised form (without surname, exact coordinates, or contact details within the research dataset). The link between the anonymised identifier and the contact information is stored separately and is accessible only for the purposes of the repeat survey (test-retest) with the additional consent of the participant.

The descriptions of the archetypes within the Dar system contain indications of “shadow sides” of the personality, which may potentially elicit an emotional response in certain participants. In connection with this:

a warning concerning the character of the content is given at the beginning of the investigation;

upon the completion of the investigation, the participant receives access to resources of psychological support (the contacts of free psychological services);

the research group undertakes to answer participants’ questions within a reasonable time.

The design of the investigation is agreed with the philosophical-methodological framework of the project (along the line of the scholarly supervisor, A. V. Makaeva).

9.8. The Current Status of the Investigation and Preliminary Results of the Pilot Phase

At the time of submission of the present monograph, the research platform nauka-yupdar.vercel.app is deployed and functioning. The basic set of measurement instrumentation has been implemented, the protocol has been agreed, the ethical framework has been approved.

The pilot phase of the investigation envisages the collection of data from 30–50 participants with detailed feedback on the operability of the platform and the intelligibility of the instrumentation. The principal task of the pilot phase is the detection of technical and methodological problems prior to the transition to the principal data collection.

Following the completion of the pilot phase and the possible correction of the instrumentation, the deployment of the principal data collection is planned, with the goal of achieving a sample volume of 500–800 participants. The results of the principal phase will be published in the form of separate scholarly articles, to which the present monograph refers as the continuation of the research programme.

The investigation laid out in this chapter is the first step in a long-term programme. The prospective directions of continuation, lying beyond the bounds of the present work, are:

the investigation of phenomena of measurable somatic effects of directed attention in work with one’s own archetype (the subject of an applied monograph);

the investigation of phenomena of user interaction depending upon their archetypal configurations;

the investigation of phenomena of social dynamics within sub-communities of YupLand;

cross-cultural investigations (in measure with the localisation of the ecosystem into other languages).

In the present chapter, a methodologically controlled design has been presented for the empirical investigation of the phenomenon of user self-recognition in the personal archetype. The design rests upon the recognition paradigm, neutralising the Barnum–Forer effect through the double-blind presentation of the own and the control descriptions of the archetype. The principal hypothesis (the proportion of recognition of one’s own archetype significantly exceeds the proportion of recognition of a random foreign one) and the auxiliary hypotheses have been formulated. The sample, the recruitment procedure, the instrumentation, the methodological controls, the plan of data analysis, and the ethical foundations of the work have been described. The empirical platform nauka-yupdar.vercel.app has been deployed and is passing the pilot phase. The final results will be published in the form of separate scholarly articles within the framework of a long-term research programme.

The empirical investigation presented in the present chapter is the first step in the empirical study of the phenomena of the Dar model and does not claim an exhaustive verification of the model as a whole. This is a deliberate methodological limitation, reflecting the orientation of the present monograph: we concentrate on the modest yet rigorous task of measuring a single, most accessible-to-empirical-work phenomenon. The unfolded programme of continuation, within which other phenomena of the embodiment of the model will also be studied, is discussed in the following — concluding — chapter.

chapters.title: Chapter 10. Conclusion. Limitations and the Programme of Further Investigations
chapters.html:
The concluding chapter of the present monograph addresses the following tasks: to generalise the results attained within the work and to fix its scholarly contribution; to indicate the methodological and substantive limitations of the work, whose open acknowledgement is necessary both as a methodological gesture and as a support for subsequent investigations; to present the programme of further investigations continuing the authorial work along both the academic and the applied directions.

10.1. The Principal Results of the Work

This monograph is the first to set out the authorial typological model Dars in a systematic academic register. The substantive contribution of the work comprises several elements, among them:

1. The philosophical-methodological framework. The distinction has been introduced and justified between the noumenal structure (the declared typology as a theoretical construct) and the phenomenological level (the observable manifestations of this structure in the experience of users of the digital ecosystem). This distinction — going back to the Kantian tradition and unfolded in the phenomenology of Husserl — has proved a productive instrument for the description of contemporary Web3 objects, to which the standard approaches of scholarly typology are not fully applicable.

2. The systematic description of the model. The three classes of archetypes have been completely described: 64 basic, 16 integral, 1 special — 81 archetypal patterns in total. Each basic archetype is described according to a unified template of 9 sections; the integrals — according to a compressed template reflecting their specificity; the archetype 9-9-9 — in an unfolded form taking account of its unique status.

3. Algorithmic formalisation. The algorithm of the generation of the individual profile from biographical parameters of the date of birth has been described and formalised, with the breakdown by the triadic structure Ma–Zhi–Kun. The algorithm is deterministic, reproducible, and observable.

4. The architectural description of the digital ecosystem. The architecture of the YupLand digital ecosystem has been described as an artifact of the embodiment of the model within the digital environment. A typology of five modes of embodiment has been introduced and operationalised (algorithmic, content, interactive, social, economic).

5. The empirical design. A methodologically controlled empirical protocol for the study of the phenomenon of user self-recognition in the personal archetype has been elaborated. The protocol employs the recognition paradigm, neutralising the Barnum–Forer effect. The protocol is realised in the form of a research platform and is deployed for the collection of data.

In addition to the substantive work, the monograph offers a methodological move possessing its own value. This move is formulated as follows: typological systems claiming to operate within the digital environment may be considered not as objects of demonstration or refutation “in principle,” but as noumenal structures whose phenomena of embodiment within a concrete digital infrastructure are accessible to empirical study. Such a posing of the question liberates the work from false expectations (“prove that the Dars exist”) without renouncing scholarly rigour (“we shall show how they manifest themselves in experience”). This methodological turn is applicable not only to the Dar model but to a wide class of contemporary typological and Web3 objects.

The monograph fixes and describes an already existing applied artifact: the YupLand digital ecosystem with the YupDar application and the research platform nauka-yupdar.vercel.app. This means that the scholarly description of the model does not precede its applied realisation but accompanies it. Such a position is characteristic of contemporary scholarship in the Web3 segment, where the academic and product contours develop in parallel. The monograph fixes this fact openly, rather than masking it.

10.2. Open Acknowledgement of Limitations

Open acknowledgement of limitations is necessary for the intellectual honesty of the work. Limitations of four types are considered: substantive, methodological, empirical, and philosophical.

Substantive limitations

The deep nature of the Dar is not disclosed. The present work concentrates on the upper, typological stratum of the model. The internal structure of each archetype, the genesis of its symbolic roots, the connection with the Zarganian sign-system — these are deliberately reserved for the programme of future works.

The hierarchy of archetypes and their interaction within the closed system is not described. The division of the 64 basic archetypes into levels of complexity and senior archetypes is a separate theme requiring its own unfolded description.

Symbolic nomination is not completed. The integral archetypes and the archetype 9-9-9 do not yet possess closed symbolic names within the authorial tradition. The search for such names is an open research task.

Application within the field of psycho-emotional self-regulation and possible correction is not disclosed. This powerful applied stratum of the model requires its own methodological and ethical grounding and belongs to future applied research work.

Methodological and empirical limitations

Self-selection of the sample. Users of YupLand and participants in the empirical investigation self-select on the basis of interest in the system. This limits the generalisability of the quantitative findings to wider populations.

The effect of the measurement artifact. Participation in the ecosystem itself forms within the user expectations that may influence his or her reactions. This effect is partially controlled within the research design but cannot be wholly eliminated.

The pilot stage. At the time of submission of the monograph, the empirical investigation is in the pilot phase. The final results will be obtained and published in separate scholarly articles.

A single object of investigation. Of the multiplicity of potentially measurable phenomena, only one is treated within the empirical part of the work — the phenomenon of self-recognition. Other phenomena (the somatic effects of directed attention, the social dynamics of sub-communities, the economic flows of the internal currency) remain the subject of future works.

Technological dependencies. The digital infrastructure depends upon external providers (hosting, language models, the messenger). This affects the reproducibility of results over time and requires the fixation of the technical versions of each stage.

Philosophical limitations

The ontological truth of the model is not demonstrated. The present work consciously does not claim to demonstrate the “real” existence of the archetypal fields or to refute alternative typological systems. The epoché with respect to this question is a methodological choice, not an intellectual capitulation.

A completed theory of consciousness is not offered. The description of the phenomena of measurable somatic effects of directed attention (mentioned in the Preface and in the empirical chapter) is not accompanied by an unfolded theoretical interpretation. This is a deliberate restraint: the corresponding theory must be constructed upon a corpus of empirical data that has yet to be gathered.

10.3. The Programme of Further Investigations

The present monograph is conceived as the first work within a series whose programme is presented below. The programme is structured along three directions — academic, applied, and infrastructural.

Academic direction

Monograph 2. The Internal Hierarchy of Archetypes. A systematic description of the levels of complexity and the senior archetypes within the Dar system; the formal typology of hierarchical connections among the basic archetypes of a single field; the discussion of possible analogues within other typological traditions.

Monograph 3. The Deep Nature of the Dar. The description of the internal structure of each archetype at the level beneath the upper typological stratum; the genesis of its symbolic roots; the analysis of the Zarganian language as the authorial sign-system.

A series of scholarly articles on the empirical work. The publication of the results of the principal phase of the empirical investigation of self-recognition (sample volume 500–800 participants); a comparative analysis of the intensity of self-recognition across the various classes of archetypes; intergroup comparisons by biographical variables; a qualitative analysis of the open-ended responses.

Comparative investigations. Publications setting the Dar model in comparison with MBTI, the Big Five, the Enneagram, and the classical astrological tradition. Each comparison requires its own methodology and must be conducted separately.

Philosophical-methodological works. The development of the methodological move of the present monograph; the application of the noumenon/phenomenon distinction to other typological systems and Web3 objects. Possible collaborations with research centres in the field of philosophy of mind.

Applied direction

Monograph “The Application of the Dars in the Field of Psycho-Emotional Self-Regulation”. The description of the authorial and pedagogical practices of work with the archetype for the regulation of psycho-emotional states; the methodological and ethical grounding of such practices; protocols for practising specialists.

Empirical investigation of the measurable somatic effects of directed attention. The recording of changes in body temperature, heart rate, and state of relaxation under conscious work with the archetypal fields. The use of standard apparatuses and protocols of biofeedback.

A psychotherapeutic protocol for bearers of the special archetype 9-9-9. The elaboration of a special protocol of work, taking account of the structural openness and the basic fear of dissolution of this archetype.

Social investigations of the YupLand community. The analysis of patterns of user interaction depending upon archetypal configurations; the investigation of phenomena of self-organisation within sub-communities.

Infrastructural direction

The development of the research platform. The extension of the functionality of nauka-yupdar.vercel.app for the conduct of additional research protocols; integration with biometric devices; localisation into other languages.

The open scholarly dataset. The publication of the anonymised dataset of the results of the empirical investigations and of the code of analysis in open access for the possibility of independent verification and reproduction.

The archive of primary sources. The systematisation and publication (in agreement with Ya. S. Sibirskiy) of the preserved records of lectures, manuscript books, and other primary sources of the Dar system in a form suited to scholarly citation.

The development of the cryptocurrency DarAi. A technical-economic investigation of the internal economy of the YupLand ecosystem; the publication of the technical documentation.

Table 10.1. A summary table of directions.

Direction

Key works

Academic

Monographs 2 and 3; scholarly articles on the empirical work; comparative and philosophical works

Applied

Monograph on psycho-emotional self-regulation; protocols; somatic investigations

Infrastructural

Development of the research platform; open dataset; archive of primary sources

10.4. Concluding Word

The present monograph is an attempt to join two perspectives that, within contemporary academic culture, rarely meet within a single text: the precise technological description of an authorial digital artifact, and the philosophical-methodological reflection upon its status. The authors are persuaded that this meeting is necessary for the adequate description of that class of objects which is being born at the boundary of the digital and the humanistic practices of the twenty-first century.

The authorial typological model Dars is one such boundary object. It is reducible neither to a purely esoteric tradition (since it is realised within a deterministic algorithm and a measurable digital infrastructure) nor to a purely scholarly typology (since its noumenal structure is declared by the author, not derived from empirical data). This boundary position requires a boundary methodology, the basic elements of which have been presented within the present work.

The authors thank the readers for their attention and invite them to substantive dialogue. Any constructive observations, objections, and developments of the ideas discussed will be taken into account in subsequent works.

The Dars are a living system, continuing to develop thanks to the work of its founder Ya. S. Sibirskiy, the authorial labour of S. N. Nesterova and the other Architects, the methodological support of the co-author A. V. Makaeva, and — in no small measure — thanks to the living work of the community of practitioners. Each of the participants in this process contributes to the common cause. The present monograph is one of the steps, and no more.

The programme of continuation presented in § 10.3 reflects the authors’ understanding that a single work cannot contain everything. Nor should it. It is sufficient if it opens a field within which subsequent steps will become possible.

With respect and gratitude,

S. N. Nesterova A. V. Makaeva

Important caveat on the use of this glossary. The etymologies provided here are offered as a heuristic aid for the English-language reader — presenting the most accessible cultural-linguistic resonances within the wider European and Eurasian traditions. They are not, however, the primary source of the Dar names. The authorial tradition holds that each Dar name issues from a deeper, multidimensional sign-system whose full elaboration is reserved for subsequent works in the series (see § 10.2 and § 10.3). The depth and richness of meaning bound up with each name exceeds what any single etymological analogy can convey; the analogies given here are intended as orientation points for the reader, not as ontological reductions of the Dar names to their cultural cognates. Readers approaching this material for the first time are encouraged to treat the table below as a doorway into the authorial language, not as a definitive interpretive key.
